title: Writing arrangements and eyesight
summary: He wrote parts for the band by day, and the group chat about not needing eyeglasses and relatives who read without them.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: His last number. Yeah, I used to do all my own writing. When I, come in, I'd sit down and write till they had to run me to bed.

Yeah, you see, sometimes work with slack at my trade, but I wasn't working in the daytime. There'd be something that didn't do. See, it rained the days, I couldn't work. Sure, it's nice. In the daytime. So, I had all day, I'd write. I'd write all that day. Write for the band. I'd write so late, tell her in the morning, she'd be running me to bed. When is you going to bed?
No, I know that those notes are small, and that's standing on the eye. And I still don't use no eyeglasses. I still don't have to use any eyeglasses.

My mother's 85, and she can pick up the newspaper, sit down there, and go in that room there, and I can't read it in that room like it is there now. And she can read that newspaper in that room there.
Well, George Lewis's mother can, too. 85 years old. She's about 94 or 5 and could do that. Her eye can.
She said, give me that. You can't see that, give me that, and she'll read it. Uh-huh, isn't that good? I don't know how they can do it.
But I can read in here. I can read anything I want in here.
I can't see with the glasses.
